key_insight: Narrow, winding collagen pores drive pressure demand, while slowly exchanging side pockets can make outlet measurements overstate interior medium replacement.
engineering_relevance: Bioreactor design should account for inlet–outlet geometry and pore connectivity to manage pumping pressure and verify effective medium renewal.
method: Simulated flow and medium replacement in pores traced from a collagen image.
Used curved-channel theory and flow resistance to estimate plug permeability.
Compared pressure demands across feeding configurations and replacement times at the outlet versus inside the pores.
evidence_signal: Simulations found roughly sevenfold higher pressure demand with small-opening feeding than uniform face feeding; in the strongest side-pocket case, interior 99% replacement took nearly three times as long as outlet replacement.
watch_item: Outlet breakthrough alone may not reliably indicate interior renewal, and image-derived pore results require validation for the target collagen plug.
paper_title: Pressure demand and solute replacement in a collagen-plugged bioreactor
